original_value: The information of building types is highly needed for urban planning and management, especially in high resolution building modeling in which buildings are the basic spatial unit. However, in many parts of the world, this information is still missing. In this paper, we proposed a framework to derive the information of building type using geospatial data, including point-of-interest (POI) data, building footprints, land use polygons, and roads, from Gaode and Baidu Maps. First, we used natural language processing (NLP)-based approaches (i.e., text similarity measurement and topic modeling) to automatically reclassify POI categories into which can be used to directly infer building types. Second, based on the relationship between building footprints and POIs, we identified building types using two indicators of type ratio and area ratio. The proposed framework was tested using over 440,000 building footprints in Beijing, China. Our NLP-based approaches and building type identification methods show overall accuracies of 89.0% and 78.2%, and kappa coefficient of 0.83 and 0.71, respectively. The proposed framework is transferrable to other China cities for deriving the information of building types from web mapping platforms. The data products generated from this study are of great use for quantitative urban studies at the building level.

result.paraphrase: Building type information is essential for urban planning and management, particularly in high-resolution building modeling where buildings serve as the basic spatial unit. Yet in many regions, such information remains unavailable. This paper presents a framework for deriving building type information from geospatial data drawn from Gaode and Baidu Maps, including point-of-interest (POI) data, building footprints, land-use polygons, and roads. First, natural language processing (NLP) methods—text similarity measurement and topic modeling—were used to automatically recategorize POI classes into categories that can directly infer building types. Second, using the relationship between building footprints and POIs, building types were identified with two indicators: type ratio and area ratio. The framework was evaluated on more than 440,000 building footprints in Beijing, China. The proposed NLP methods and building type identification methods achieved overall accuracies of 89.0% and 78.2%, with kappa coefficients of 0.83 and 0.71, respectively. The framework is transferable to other Chinese cities for extracting building type information from web mapping platforms. The resulting data products are highly valuable for quantitative urban studies at the building level.
